#Padres 

Cesar Rizik -> Senior Director, Latin America Operations

Since coming over from the #Astros -> Kris Gross has focused a lot of time & resources to strengthening our sphere of influence within the Dominican Republic. 

James Kang & Laiky Uribe have worked well with Gross to position the #Mets as favorites to steal Wandy Asigen when the opportunity presented itself & lock-up Euniel De La Cruz after losing Alfredo Sena to the #Braves. 

There’s no denying the #SFGiants, #Brewers, & #Padres are arguably the only teams who have matched the #Mets ability to land top I.F.A. talent over the last 3 years, they’ve done a great job of securing Big $ signings & high impact players for under $2 Million. 

An area the #Mets have not had as much success in & adding any of the executives listed above would be a huge boost.

#Mets 2026 - 2027 Off-season Blueprint:

To build a sustainable winner, #Mets leadership has to re-calibrate their Roster Build approach & commit to a few changes:

Even if it takes them 1 or 2 years to fully develop the players who can help them become a perennial playoff team, the wait will be worth it & they’ll save tens of millions annually:

Organizational Mandate -> Engage the Youth Movement:

A. Commit to younger players -> who deserve time to develop:

Younger players who flashed impact potential in 2026, need to become the anchors for our 2027 Roster:

Top Prospects who are primed to graduate within a year, should not be blocked by expensive veterans.

B. It’s time to abandon -> expensive reclamation projects:

Buying low on a Griffin Canning type ($3M salary in 2025), I get it, but spending $20M on a player, hoping he regains his form from 3 years ago is a ridiculous approach & too risky.

For every “Chris Sale success story -> there are at least 6-8 examples where it backfired, a lot of those cases on our roster

C. Maintain roster flexibility -> “don’t go chasing waterfalls” 

Chasing success in the short-term to appease fans has not worked for 40 years & counting.

Create a plan focused on developing homegrown talent & stick to it & if you have the chance to acquire an ELITE talent, who can help develop younger players, go all in to sign them

Spending $15-$25 million for Tier II players -> has become antiquated & is no longer guaranteeing success.

Spending that kind of money for Tier III players -> as an attempt to avoid having to dish out 4-5 year deals is even worse & has proven to be a CATASTROPHIC approach.

D. Trade Market has become cost-prohibitive & overpaying for rental players has become too expensive for Big Market Clubs:

#TBRays getting to acquire Peralta for less than what the #Mets had to fork over for Ryan Helsley isn’t bad luck, it’s the new industry norm -> we won’t win these trades going forward 

“Buy-Low” acquisitions that fill a short-term roster need or “Sell-High” trades that create roster space for Top Prospects

#LGM
